"Adorned with all the marks" means adorned with the major and minor marks. The "ten powers" are the power of knowing what is possible and impossible, and so forth. The "fearlessnesses" are four; likewise, the "and so forth" refers to being endowed with the qualities of a Buddha, such as the faculties, powers, limbs of enlightenment, and limbs of the path. The distinction of that is the completion of the **Great Seal**, the nature of the body of **Vajrasattva**. Through such phrases, the benefits of attaining reality are shown. "The three realms" means having attained the Buddhahood of the three worlds, one bestows the result of the desired goal. Likewise, the "highly renowned marks" are the unique applications of mindfulness and so forth. Through the phrase "a hundred leagues" <term>yojana</term> and so forth, it is shown that one will illuminate the world-realms of one's own **Infinite Light** <term>Amitābha</term>. Likewise, through the meditative concentration of union, which is the inseparable essence of the conventional and the ultimate, it is shown that one performs the peaceful activities and so forth for the benefit of beings. Through the phrase "just explained" and so forth, the non-transgression of the meditative concentration of the completion stage is shown. Regarding "the practitioner" and so forth, through the meditative concentration of withdrawal via the proximity of the faculties and the sense-objects, the "unlocalized nirvana" which is illustrated by the clear light means the reality of the nature of union. "Peace" means being free from all elaborations. Because the fulfillment of the benefit of others is primary, one should adopt virtue. Because reality is unmistakable, it is "unfailing." The **Compiler** has shown that one will attain the "preeminent," which is the chief among worldly and transcendent accomplishments.

yogi." So it appears. Thus, the text has shown the experience of the Clear Light through the internal and external sequences of manifest enlightenment, and the radiation of the Vajra Body arising from that. 

Regarding "adorned with all the marks," this means adorned with the primary and secondary marks of a Buddha. The "ten powers" are the "knowledge of what is possible and impossible" and so forth. "Fearlessnesses" are four. Similarly, by the word "and so forth," one possesses the qualities of a Buddha such as the faculties, powers, branches of enlightenment, and branches of the path. Its distinction is the perfection of the Great Seal, which is the nature of the body of **Vajrasattva**. 

By the phrase "thus" and so forth, the benefits of obtaining reality are shown. "The three realms" means that by obtaining the Buddhahood of the three worlds, one bestows the fruit through the desired goals. Similarly, "the renowned marks" are those who possess the unique "applications of mindfulness" and so forth. By the phrase "a hundred leagues" <term>yojana</term> and so forth, it is shown that one will illuminate the world-realms of one's own infinite light. Similarly, it is shown that through the meditative concentration of union, which is the inseparable essence of the conventional and ultimate, one performs activities for the sake of beings such as "pacifying" and so forth. 

By the phrase "just explained" and so forth, it is shown that one does not deviate from the meditative concentration of the completion stage. Regarding "the practitioner" and so forth: whoever, by means of the meditative concentration of "individual withdrawal" through the gateway of the senses and the usage of objects, illustrates the Clear Light—that reality which is non-abiding nirvana, the essence of union, is peace. It is free from all elaborations. Because the welfare of others is the primary goal, one should take up virtue. Because that reality is unerring, it is "non-deceptive." The compiler shows that because it is the chief of worldly and transworldly attainments, one will obtain the "most excellent."
